options: A single physical server dedicated to one AWS customer
An isolated, private network you define inside an AWS Region, with its own address space
A synonym for an Availability Zone
A billing construct with no actual networking function
questions.explain: A VPC is the isolated private network AWS customers define inside a Region — the foundation almost everything else runs inside.

questions.q: How does a subnet relate to a VPC and to Availability Zones?
options: A VPC can only ever contain exactly one subnet
A subnet spans every Availability Zone in the Region simultaneously
A subnet is a slice of the VPC's address range, and each subnet lives in exactly one Availability Zone
Subnets and VPCs are two names for the same thing
questions.explain: Unlike the VPC (which spans a Region), each individual subnet is confined to one Availability Zone.

questions.q: What actually determines whether a subnet is 'public' or 'private'?
options: The subnet's CIDR block size
Whether the subnet contains an EC2 instance or not
Its route table — a public subnet's route table sends internet-bound traffic to an Internet Gateway, a private subnet's doesn't
A checkbox labeled 'public' set when the subnet is created, with no other effect
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that it's the route table's route to an Internet Gateway that makes a subnet public, not a simple label.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a security group and a network ACL (NACL)?
options: A security group is a stateful firewall attached to a resource; a NACL is a stateless firewall applied at the subnet level
Security groups and NACLs are two names for exactly the same feature
A NACL is stateful and a security group is stateless
NACLs can only be used inside a public subnet
questions.explain: Security groups are stateful and resource-level; NACLs are stateless and subnet-level — a coarser backstop.

questions.q: What does 'stateful' mean in the context of a security group?
options: It only applies to traffic within a single Availability Zone
If inbound traffic on a port is allowed, the matching outbound response is automatically allowed too, without a separate rule
The security group remembers every IP address that has ever connected, permanently
It requires a database to store its rules externally
questions.explain: Statefulness means the return traffic for an allowed request doesn't need its own explicit rule — unlike a stateless NACL.
